claims.text: H2 blocker if PPIs are unavailable or can't be used; ⍉ acid suppressants just for crying/distress and/or visible regurgitation.
claims.quote: If PPIs are unavailable or cannot be used, an H2 blocker can be given. These medications are not recommended simply for treatment of crying/distress and/or visible regurgitation.

claims.text: Promotility drugs ⍉ first-line; baclofen may be tried before surgery in infants unresponsive to acid blockers;
claims.quote: The North American and European specialty societies recommend against use of promotility medications as first-line treatment, although baclofen may be tried before performing surgery on infants who are unresponsive to acid-blocking medications
Bethanechol, domperidone, and metoclopramide are not recommended because of their potential adverse effects.
